finding.claim: The /checkout route computes the charge from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set price to a tiny value, or price or qty to a negative number, so the total is near zero or negative. That means free goods, or a negative charge that may act as a refund or credit, depending on the payments backend. The sibling /checkout-v2 looks prices up server-side and clamps qty, which shows this route is the unsafe one.

trace.note: POST /checkout handler takes req.body.items with no schema validation
total = sum of i.price * i.qty, using the client-supplied values directly
the total is charged to the user and returned in the response

finding.guards_checked: There is no server-side price lookup, no numeric or positive validation, and no qty clamp on this route. Only cart.js exists in the directory, so I could not see any middleware that might validate the body. /checkout-v2 (lines 10-18) does have these controls (catalog.price lookup and Math.max(1, Math.floor(qty))), so it is SAFE for this issue.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no lookup, positivity check or clamp, and cart.js:6 charges that total for any authenticated user (req.user.id), whereas /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14) does the server-side lookup and clamp. Only cart.js exists, so upstream middleware can't be seen, but nothing in the route validates the body.
